subject: Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) when using stat_bin

messages.author: ea7c5cb34f4d965b
messages.subject: Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) when using stat_bin
parts:
Hello,

I'm relatively new to R and very new to ggplot2. I've been playing and
simply trying to recreate this this example of a map colored by bins
(the eighth image down) which reads as follows:

> cars + stat_bin(aes(fill=..count..), geom="tile", binwidth=3,
+ position="identity")

on this page http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_tile.html

He is my code:

mycsv<- read.csv("~/Desktop/sample_data.csv", header=TRUE, sep=",")
myplot <- ggplot(mycsv, aes(y=column1, x=column2))
myplot + stat_bin(aes(fill=..count..), geom="tile", binwidth=3,
position="identity")

The CSV is structured:

column1 column2 column3
45 42 53
87 31 83
78 77 78
56 68 42
44 97 27
74 43 14
82 2 31
7 38 34
56 28 96
...

It's returning:

Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'y' not found

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) when using stat_bin
parts:
What you've left out from the geom_tile() page is what "cars" is... 

ggplot(mtcars, aes(y=factor(cyl), x=mpg)) 

The important part is the factor(). When I added y=as.factor(column1), it plotted. The plot is fairly non-sensical since it's likely that each of your column 1 values are fairly unique. 

HTH, Brandon

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) when using stat_bin
parts:
Hi:

Take another look at geom_tile() and some of the examples on its page,
especially toward the bottom: http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_tile.html
As Brandon pointed out, the structure of the data you pass to the geom
affects the type of output you get.

You might also want to look at the help page of stat_bin2d() if you
need to bin both vertically and horizontally. There are various ways
to control color gradients, too; see the help page of
scale_gradientn() for some examples.

Dennis
